thread.title: Earnings Outlook: Qualcomm earnings: Last peek before investors decide fate of standalone company

title: Earnings Outlook: Qualcomm earnings: Last peek before investors decide fate of standalone company

organizations.name: mages wallace witkowski reporter  qualcomm inc.

text:
Qualcomm Inc. earnings are expected to serve as a gauge for investors to decide whether the chip maker will remain an independent company as it heads into its annual shareholder meeting in March.
Much of Qualcomm’s QCOM, -0.57% quarter has been dominated by what has become a hostile takeover attempt by Broadcom Ltd. AVGO, -1.44% to acquire the company. Recently, Qualcomm made a pitch for its value as a stand-alone company, announcing a $1 billion cost-reduction program and forecast adjusted earnings of $6.75 to $7.50 a share for fiscal 2019. 
Earlier in the month, Qualcomm sent a letter to shareholders urging them to reject the takeover bid from Broadcom. In December, Broadcom nominated a slate of directors to completely replace Qualcomm’s board . As far back as November, analysts have not been too optimistic about such a deal going through . 
See also: Qualcomm issues go beyond Apple fight 
The company also needs to still sort through litigation with Apple Inc. AAPL, -1.08% . Last week, the European Union fined Qualcomm $1.23 billion , or €997 million, for illegal payments made to Apple to use its chips exclusively in smartphones. Apple sued Qualcomm a year ago , claiming that it was using patents to extract unreasonable royalties, and it has been a constant focus in earnings calls ever since . 
Expect more chatter about Apple and Broadcom when Qualcomm announces fiscal first-quarter earnings after the bell on Wednesday. 
What to expect 
Earnings: Of the 18 analysts surveyed by FactSet, Qualcomm on average is expected to post adjusted earnings of 91 cents a share. Qualcomm forecast 85 cents to 95 cents a share. Estimize, a software platform that uses crowdsourcing from hedge-fund executives, brokerages, buy-side analysts and others, calls for earnings of 93 cents a share.
Revenue: Wall Street expects revenue of $5.92 billion from Qualcomm, according to 14 analysts polled by FactSet. That’s up from the $5.89 billion forecast at the beginning of the quarter. Qualcomm predicted revenue of $5.5 billion to $6.3 billion. Estimize expects revenue of $6 billion.
Stock movement: Qualcomm shares are up 5.2% for the year, following a 1.8% decline in 2017. In comparison, the PHLX Semiconductor Index SOX, -1.71% is up 10% this year, and gained 38% in 2017, while the S&P 500 index SPX, -0.90% is up 6.7% this year after a 2017 gain of about 20%.
What analysts are saying 
On Monday, RBC Capital analyst Amit Daryanani, who has an outperform rating, raised his price target to $80 from $77 on the probability that Qualcomm will submit to a higher offer from Broadcom as the March 6 shareholder meeting approaches. What remains to be seen is how Qualcomm clears the last of regulatory hurdles for its own acquisition of NXP Semiconductors NXPI, -0.38% 
We think high probability that QCOM will spend time convincing shareholders during their EPS call and beyond on their ability to achieve $6.00+ EPS (noted potential for $6.75-7.50 post AAPL resolution) and execute on cost take out initiatives. 
Canaccord analyst T. Michael Walkley, who has a buy rating and an $86 price target, said Qualcomm is making its case to remain an independent company. He noted:
While we expected management would present its case to investors to remain independent, we are encouraged by the new $1B cost reduction program. We also believe Qualcomm’s acquisition of NXP remains on track and will create a company with significant earnings power and cash flow, developing into a clear industry leader in the mobile, IoT, and automotive semiconductor markets backed by the extremely strong combined IP portfolio of Qualcomm, NXP, and Freescale (Motorola).
Susquehanna Financial analyst Christopher Rolland, who has a positive rating and a $78 price target, said it was interesting that Qualcomm management took the announced outlook to note that its auto, Internet of Things, datacenter and other businesses are expected to contribute $7 billion to $8 billion in revenue in fiscal 2019, and that Qualcomm’s 2019 target seems achievable whether it acquires NXP or not.
Of the 22 analysts who cover Qualcomm, 10 have buy or overweight ratings, 12 have hold ratings and none have sell or underweight ratings, with an average price target of $69.25, or nearly 3% higher than Monday’s close.
